jobs.source:
# frozen_string_literal: true

module FddJob__
  extend ::FddRuntime

  def self.sign_in(request, deps)
    __f = ::FddVerify.frame("bp-auth-login")
    __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-001")
    email = get(get(request, "body"), "email")
    email_check = check_email(email, "email")
    password = get(get(request, "body"), "password")
    __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-006")
    if !(bool(get(email_check, "valid")) && !is_empty(password))
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-009")
      return obj(
        "status", 401.0,
        "body", obj(
          "error", bool(get(email_check, "valid")) ? get(check_required(password, "password"), "message") : get(email_check, "message")
        )
      )
    end
    __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-010")
    look_up_user = ::FddVerify.dep("userService", "getUsersByEmail", "NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-010", [obj("query", omit_nulls(obj("email", email)))])
    status1 = get(look_up_user, "status")
    if eq(status1, 200.0)
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-014")
      if !eq(get(get(look_up_user, "body"), "passwordHash"), format("hash:{password}", obj("password", password)))
        __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-021")
        return obj("status", 401.0, "body", obj("error", "Invalid credentials"))
      end
      id = get(get(look_up_user, "body"), "id")
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-018")
      ::FddVerify.dep("eventBus", "publishUserLoggedIn", "NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-018", [obj("userId", id)])
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-019")
      return obj(
        "status", 200.0,
        "body", obj(
          "accessToken", format("TEST-TOKEN-{id}", obj("id", id)),
          "refreshToken", "REFRESH-TOKEN",
          "expiresIn", 3600.0,
          "tokenType", "Bearer"
        )
      )
    elsif eq(status1, 404.0)
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-022")
      return obj("status", 401.0, "body", obj("error", "Invalid credentials"))
    else
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-023")
      raise FddError.new("UPSTREAM_ERROR", "User Service failed")
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Runtime for code generated by Rabbinatix from Logic Blueprints. Do not edit: it is regenerated on export.
# Every helper mirrors the simulator, so generated handlers behave exactly like their blueprints.

require 'digest'

# the helpers, the errors and the JSON conversions
module FddRuntime
  # An error with a code, like the simulator's errors (Throw nodes, DIVIDE_BY_ZERO, INVALID_JSON...).
  class FddError < StandardError
    attr_reader :code

    def initialize(code, message)
      @code = FddRuntime.as_string(code)
      super(FddRuntime.as_string(message))
    end
  end

  # An error that stops a handler: Try and Retry never catch it.
  module FddStop
  end

  # A path that isn't there (JavaScript's undefined): left out of objects, like JSON.stringify does.
  MISSING = Object.new.freeze

  # Converts between your own values and the JSON values the handlers take and return.
  module FddJson
    # Hashes (any keys), arrays, numbers of any type and objects with to_value or to_h as JSON values.
    def self.to_value(v)
      case v
      when nil, String, true, false then v
      when Numeric then v.to_f
      when Symbol then v.to_s
      when Hash then v.each_with_object({}) { |(k, x), o| o[k.to_s] = to_value(x) }
      when Array then v.map { |x| to_value(x) }
      else
        return to_value(v.to_value) if v.respond_to?(:to_value)
        return to_value(v.to_h) if v.respond_to?(:to_h)

        v.to_s
      end
    end

    # JSON text as JSON values; fails with FddError INVALID_JSON.
    def self.parse(text)
      JsonReader.new(text).document
    end

    # JSON values as JSON text (JSON.stringify).
    def self.stringify(v)
      FddRuntime.json(v)
    end
  end

  # Strict JSON (what JSON.parse accepts); numbers become floats.
  class JsonReader
    def initialize(text)
      @s = text.b
      @i = 0
    end

    def document
      ws
      v = value
      ws
      raise bad unless @i == @s.bytesize

      v
    end

    private

    def bad
      FddError.new('INVALID_JSON', 'Not valid JSON')
    end

    def ws
      @i += 1 while @i < @s.bytesize && " \t\n\r".include?(@s[@i])
    end

    def peek
      raise bad if @i >= @s.bytesize

      @s[@i]
    end

    def value
      c = peek
      return object if c == '{'
      return array if c == '['
      return string if c == '"'

      { 'true' => true, 'false' => false, 'null' => nil }.each do |w, v|
        if @s.byteslice(@i, w.bytesize) == w
          @i += w.bytesize
          return v
        end
      end
      m = /\G-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?/n.match(@s, @i)
      raise bad unless m && m.begin(0) == @i

      @i += m[0].bytesize
      m[0].to_f
    end

    def object
      o = {}
      @i += 1
      ws
      if peek == '}'
        @i += 1
        return o
      end
      loop do
        ws
        raise bad unless peek == '"'

        k = string
        ws
        raise bad unless peek == ':'

        @i += 1
        ws
        o[k] = value
        ws
        c = peek
        @i += 1
        return o if c == '}'
        raise bad unless c == ','
      end
    end

    def array
      l = []
      @i += 1
      ws
      if peek == ']'
        @i += 1
        return l
      end
      loop do
        ws
        l << value
        ws
        c = peek
        @i += 1
        return l if c == ']'
        raise bad unless c == ','
      end
    end

    SIMPLE = { '"' => '"', '\\' => '\\', '/' => '/', 'b' => "\b", 'f' => "\f", 'n' => "\n", 'r' => "\r", 't' => "\t" }.freeze

    def string
      @i += 1
      units = []
      out = String.new(encoding: Encoding::BINARY)
      loop do
        c = peek
        @i += 1
        if c == '"'
          out << FddRuntime.from_units(units).b unless units.empty?
          return out.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
        end
        raise bad if c.ord < 0x20

        if c != '\\'
          unless units.empty?
            out << FddRuntime.from_units(units).b
            units = []
          end
          out << c
          next
        end
        e = peek
        @i += 1
        if SIMPLE.key?(e)
          unless units.empty?
            out << FddRuntime.from_units(units).b
            units = []
          end
          out << SIMPLE[e]
          next
        end
        hex = @s.byteslice(@i, 4)
        raise bad unless e == 'u' && hex =~ /\A[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\z/

        @i += 4
        # \u escapes are UTF-16 units: a pair becomes one character
        units << hex.to_i(16)
      end
    end
  end

  module_function

  # ---------- text as UTF-16 units ----------

  # The UTF-16 units of UTF-8 text (a lone surrogate written as its own 3 bytes stays one unit).
  def units(s)
    b = s.b
    out = []
    n = b.bytesize
    i = 0
    while i < n
      x = b.getbyte(i)
      if x < 0x80
        cp = x
        i += 1
      elsif x < 0xe0 && i + 1 < n
        cp = ((x & 0x1f) << 6) | (b.getbyte(i + 1) & 0x3f)
        i += 2
      elsif x < 0xf0 && i + 2 < n
        cp = ((x & 0x0f) << 12) | ((b.getbyte(i + 1) & 0x3f) << 6) | (b.getbyte(i + 2) & 0x3f)
        i += 3
      elsif i + 3 < n
        cp = ((x & 0x07) << 18) | ((b.getbyte(i + 1) & 0x3f) << 12) | ((b.getbyte(i + 2) & 0x3f) << 6) | (b.getbyte(i + 3) & 0x3f)
        i += 4
      else
        cp = 0xfffd
        i += 1
      end
      if cp >= 0x10000
        cp -= 0x10000
        out << (0xd800 | (cp >> 10)) << (0xdc00 | (cp & 0x3ff))
      else
        out << cp
      end
    end
    out
  end

  # UTF-16 units as UTF-8 text (pairs joined; a lone surrogate as its own 3 bytes).
  def from_units(u)
    out = String.new(encoding: Encoding::BINARY)
    i = 0
    n = u.length
    while i < n
      c = u[i]
      if c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff && i + 1 < n && u[i + 1] >= 0xdc00 && u[i + 1] <= 0xdfff
        c = 0x10000 + ((c - 0xd800) << 10) + (u[i + 1] - 0xdc00)
        i += 1
      end
      if c < 0x80
        out << c
      elsif c < 0x800
        out << (0xc0 | (c >> 6)) << (0x80 | (c & 0x3f))
      elsif c < 0x10000
        out << (0xe0 | (c >> 12)) << (0x80 | ((c >> 6) & 0x3f)) << (0x80 | (c & 0x3f))
      else
        out << (0xf0 | (c >> 18)) << (0x80 | ((c >> 12) & 0x3f)) << (0x80 | ((c >> 6) & 0x3f)) << (0x80 | (c & 0x3f))
      end
      i += 1
    end
    out.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
  end

  # the position of a text in another, in UTF-16 units, or -1
  def unit_index(t, s)
    (0..(t.length - s.length)).each { |i| return i if t[i, s.length] == s }
    -1
  end

  # ---------- the value model the generated code uses ----------

  # A condition: true only for true, else JavaScript truthiness.
  def bool(v)
    v == true || (v != false && truthy(v))
  end

  # A number operand.
  def num(v)
    to_num(v)
  end

  # o.name, null-safe: nil when o is nil or has no such field.
  def get(o, name)
    key_of(o, name)
  end

  # o[key], null-safe.
  def item(o, k)
    key_of(o, k)
  end

  # An object from key, value, key, value...
  def obj(*kv)
    o = {}
    kv.each_slice(2) { |k, v| o[k] = v }
    o
  end

  # a === b for strings, numbers, booleans and nil (objects and lists: the same one).
  def eq(a, b)
    return a.to_f == b.to_f if a.is_a?(Numeric) && b.is_a?(Numeric)
    return a.equal?(b) if a.is_a?(Hash) || a.is_a?(Array)

    a == b && a.class == b.class
  end

  # a % b (JavaScript's remainder: the sign of a).
  def mod(a, b)
    return Float::NAN if b.zero? || a.infinite? || a.nan? || b.nan?
    return a if b.infinite?

    a.remainder(b)
  end

  # a ?? b: b runs only when a is nil.
  def coalesce(a)
    a.nil? ? yield : a
  end

  def iter(v)
    v.is_a?(Array) ? v : []
  end

  # [index, item] of a list; the index is a number.
  def indexed(v)
    iter(v).each_with_index.map { |x, i| [i.to_f, x] }
  end

  # from, from + 1, ... while at most to.
  def range(from, to)
    Enumerator.new do |y|
      i = from
      while i <= to
        y << i
        i += 1
      end
    end
  end

  # from, from + 1, ... without end (the loop stops itself).
  def counting(from)
    Enumerator.new do |y|
      i = from
      loop do
        y << i
        i += 1
      end
    end
  end

  def map(items)
    as_array(items).each_with_index.map { |x, i| yield(x, i.to_f) }
  end

  def filter(items)
    as_array(items).each_with_index.select { |x, i| yield(x, i.to_f) }.map(&:first)
  end

  def find(items)
    as_array(items).each_with_index { |x, i| return x if yield(x, i.to_f) }
    nil
  end

  def some(items)
    as_array(items).each_with_index { |x, i| return true if yield(x, i.to_f) }
    false
  end

  def every(items)
    as_array(items).each_with_index { |x, i| return false unless yield(x, i.to_f) }
    true
  end

  # One item at a time (deterministic order).
  def map_async(items, &fn)
    map(items, &fn)
  end

  def filter_async(items)
    filter(items) { |x, i| truthy(yield(x, i)) }
  end

  def find_async(items)
    find(items) { |x, i| truthy(yield(x, i)) }
  end

  def some_async(items)
    some(items) { |x, i| truthy(yield(x, i)) }
  end

  def every_async(items)
    every(items) { |x, i| truthy(yield(x, i)) }
  end

  def key_of(o, k)
    case o
    when Hash then o[k.is_a?(String) ? k : js_string(k)]
    when Array
      return o.length.to_f if k == 'length'

      i = list_index(k)
      i >= 0 && i < o.length ? o[i] : nil
    when String
      u = units(o)
      return u.length.to_f if k == 'length'

      i = list_index(k)
      i >= 0 && i < u.length ? from_units([u[i]]) : nil
    end
  end

  # A list position, or -1.
  def list_index(k)
    d = if k.is_a?(Numeric) then k.to_f
        elsif k.is_a?(String) && k.match?(/\A[0-9]+\z/) then k.to_f
        else return -1
        end
    d >= 0 && d < 2_147_483_647 && d.floor == d ? d.to_i : -1
  end

  def trunc(d)
    d.finite? ? d.truncate.to_f : d
  end

  # ---------- JavaScript conversions ----------

  # A number as JavaScript's String(n) writes it.
  def num_text(n)
    n = n.to_f
    return 'NaN' if n.nan?
    return n.positive? ? 'Infinity' : '-Infinity' if n.infinite?
    return '0' if n.zero?

    # Float#to_s has the shortest digits that read back as the same number
    mant, exp = n.abs.to_s.split('e')
    int, frac = mant.split('.')
    all = int + (frac || '')
    lead = all[/\A0*/].length
    digits = all[lead..].sub(/0+\z/, '')
    digits = '0' if digits.empty?
    point = int.length + exp.to_i - lead
    k = digits.length
    sign = n.negative? ? '-' : ''
    return sign + digits + ('0' * (point - k)) if k <= point && point <= 21
    return "#{sign}#{digits[0, point]}.#{digits[point..]}" if point.positive? && point <= 21
    return "#{sign}0.#{'0' * -point}#{digits}" if -6 < point && point <= 0

    x = point - 1
    "#{sign}#{digits[0]}#{k > 1 ? ".#{digits[1..]}" : ''}e#{x >= 0 ? '+' : '-'}#{x.abs}"
  end

  # String(v).
  def js_string(v)
    case v
    when nil then 'null'
    when true then 'true'
    when false then 'false'
    when Numeric then num_text(v)
    when String then v
    when Array then v.map { |x| x.nil? ? '' : js_string(x) }.join(',')
    when Hash then '[object Object]'
    when Exception then v.message
    else v.to_s
    end
  end

  # JSON.stringify.
  def json(v)
    case v
    when nil then 'null'
    when true then 'true'
    when false then 'false'
    when Numeric then v.to_f.finite? ? num_text(v) : 'null'
    when String then quote(v)
    when Array then "[#{v.map { |x| json(x) }.join(',')}]"
    when Hash then "{#{key_list(v).map { |k| "#{quote(k)}:#{json(v[k])}" }.join(',')}}"
    else quote(js_string(v))
    end
  end

  ESCAPES = { 0x22 => '\\"', 0x5c => '\\\\', 0x0a => '\\n', 0x0d => '\\r', 0x09 => '\\t', 0x08 => '\\b', 0x0c => '\\f' }.freeze

  def quote(s)
    out = String.new('"')
    u = units(s)
    n = u.length
    i = 0
    while i < n
      c = u[i]
      if ESCAPES.key?(c)
        out << ESCAPES[c]
      elsif c < 0x20
        out << format_hex(c)
      elsif c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff && i + 1 < n && u[i + 1] >= 0xdc00 && u[i + 1] <= 0xdfff
        out << from_units([c, u[i + 1]])
        i += 1
      elsif c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdfff
        out << format_hex(c)
      else
        out << from_units([c])
      end
      i += 1
    end
    out << '"'
  end

  def format_hex(c)
    "\\u#{c.to_s(16).rjust(4, '0')}"
  end

  # JavaScript's white space and line terminators (what String.prototype.trim removes).
  JS_SPACE = "[\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000\\ufeff]"
  TRIM_RE = Regexp.new("\\A#{JS_SPACE}+|#{JS_SPACE}+\\z")

  def js_trim(s)
    s.valid_encoding? ? s.gsub(TRIM_RE, '') : s.strip
  end

  # Number(v).
  def js_number(v)
    case v
    when nil then 0.0
    when true then 1.0
    when false then 0.0
    when Numeric then v.to_f
    when String
      t = js_trim(v)
      return 0.0 if t.empty?

      if (m = /\A0([xXoObB])([0-9a-fA-F]+)\z/.match(t))
        radix = { 'x' => 16, 'o' => 8, 'b' => 2 }[m[1].downcase]
        return Float::NAN unless m[2].chars.all? { |c| c.to_i(16) < radix && c.match?(/[0-9a-fA-F]/) }

        return m[2].to_i(radix).to_f
      end
      return Float::INFINITY if ['Infinity', '+Infinity'].include?(t)
      return -Float::INFINITY if t == '-Infinity'

      t.match?(/\A[+-]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?\z/) ? Float(t.sub(/\A([+-]?)\./, '\10.').sub(/\.(?=[eE]|\z)/, '')) : Float::NAN
    when Array
      return 0.0 if v.empty?
      return Float::NAN if v.length > 1

      x = v[0]
      x.is_a?(Array) || x.is_a?(Hash) ? Float::NAN : (x.nil? ? 0.0 : js_number(x))
    else Float::NAN
    end
  end

  def prim(x)
    x.is_a?(Array) || x.is_a?(Hash) ? js_string(x) : x
  end

  def lt(a, b)
    return (units(a) <=> units(b)).negative? if a.is_a?(String) && b.is_a?(String)

    js_number(prim(a)) < js_number(prim(b))
  end

  # ---------- values ----------

  # Branch semantics: "" and "false" are false.
  def truthy(v)
    case v
    when nil, false then false
    when String then !v.empty? && v != 'false'
    when Numeric then !v.zero? && !(v.is_a?(Float) && v.nan?)
    else true
    end
  end

  # nil, "", [] or {}.
  def is_empty(v)
    case v
    when nil then true
    when String then js_trim(v).empty?
    when Array, Hash then v.empty?
    else false
    end
  end

  # nil or missing.
  def is_null(v)
    v.nil?
  end

  # Structural equality (objects and arrays by value).
  def deep_equal(a, b)
    return a.to_f == b.to_f || (a.to_f.nan? && b.to_f.nan?) if a.is_a?(Numeric) && b.is_a?(Numeric)
    return a.length == b.length && a.each_index.all? { |i| deep_equal(a[i], b[i]) } if a.is_a?(Array) && b.is_a?(Array)
    return a.length == b.length && a.all? { |k, x| b.key?(k) && deep_equal(x, b[k]) } if a.is_a?(Hash) && b.is_a?(Hash)

    eq(a, b)
  end

  # -1, 0 or 1.
  def compare(a, b)
    return 0.0 if deep_equal(a, b)

    lt(a, b) ? -1.0 : 1.0
  end

  # An arithmetic operand: numbers as is, anything else through Number().
  def to_num(v)
    v.is_a?(Float) ? v : (v.is_a?(Numeric) ? v.to_f : js_number(v))
  end

  # Fails on zero.
  def divide(a, b)
    raise FddError.new('DIVIDE_BY_ZERO', 'Division by zero') if to_num(b).zero?

    to_num(a) / to_num(b)
  end

  # The value if it is a list, else [].
  def as_array(v)
    v.is_a?(Array) ? v : []
  end

  # A query found something (not nil, not an empty list).
  def is_found(v)
    v.is_a?(Array) ? !v.empty? : !v.nil?
  end

  # Drops nil entries (query and header maps).
  def omit_nulls(o)
    o.is_a?(Hash) ? key_list(o).each_with_object({}) { |k, out| out[k] = o[k] unless o[k].nil? } : {}
  end

  # ---------- paths & objects ----------

  # user.roles[0].name → [["user", -1], ["roles", -1], [nil, 0], ["name", -1]]
  def segments(path)
    path.split('.').reject(&:empty?).flat_map do |part|
      part.scan(/([^\[\]]+)|\[(\d+)\]/).map { |name, idx| name ? [name, -1] : [nil, idx.length > 9 ? 2_147_483_647 : idx.to_i] }
    end
  end

  def seg_key(s)
    s[0] || s[1].to_s
  end

  def unsafe(segs)
    segs.any? { |s| ['__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype'].include?(s[0]) }
  end

  # The path exists (its value may be nil).
  def has_path(value, path)
    p = str(path)
    return true if p.empty? || p == '$'

    segs = segments(p)
    return false if unsafe(segs)

    cur = value
    segs.each do |s|
      if cur.is_a?(Hash)
        return false unless cur.key?(seg_key(s))

        cur = cur[seg_key(s)]
      elsif cur.is_a?(Array) || cur.is_a?(String)
        n = cur.is_a?(Array) ? cur.length : units(cur).length
        if s[0] == 'length' then cur = n.to_f
        elsif s[0].nil? && s[1] < n then cur = key_of(cur, s[1])
        else return false
        end
      else
        return false
      end
    end
    true
  end

  # Reads a nested value; nil when a step is missing.
  def get_path(value, path)
    p = str(path)
    return value if p.empty? || p == '$'

    segs = segments(p)
    return nil if unsafe(segs)

    cur = value
    segs.each do |s|
      return nil if cur.nil?

      cur = key_of(cur, s[0] || s[1].to_f)
    end
    cur
  end

  def lookup(value, path)
    has_path(value, path) ? get_path(value, path) : MISSING
  end

  def container(v)
    v.is_a?(Array) || v.is_a?(Hash)
  end

  def shallow(v)
    container(v) ? v.dup : v
  end

  # A copy with a nested value set.
  def set_path(value, path, v)
    segs = segments(str(path))
    return v if segs.empty?

    root = container(value) ? shallow(value) : {}
    return root if unsafe(segs)

    set_in(root, segs, 0, v)
    root
  end

  # Sets segs[i..] in cur, a fresh copy.
  def set_in(cur, segs, i, v)
    s = segs[i]
    last = i == segs.length - 1
    if cur.is_a?(Array)
      return unless s[0].nil?

      cur << nil while cur.length <= s[1]
      if last
        cur[s[1]] = v unless v.equal?(MISSING)
        return
      end
      nxt = shallow(cur[s[1]])
      nxt = segs[i + 1][0].nil? ? [] : {} unless container(nxt)
      cur[s[1]] = nxt
      set_in(nxt, segs, i + 1, v)
      return
    end
    k = seg_key(s)
    if last
      cur[k] = v unless v.equal?(MISSING)
      return
    end
    nxt = cur.key?(k) ? shallow(cur[k]) : nil
    nxt = segs[i + 1][0].nil? ? [] : {} unless container(nxt)
    cur[k] = nxt
    set_in(nxt, segs, i + 1, v)
  end

  def deep_clone(v)
    case v
    when Array then v.map { |x| deep_clone(x) }
    when Hash then v.to_h { |k, x| [k, deep_clone(x)] }
    else v
    end
  end

  # A copy without a nested value.
  def remove_path(value, path)
    segs = segments(str(path))
    return value if segs.empty? || !container(value)

    clone = deep_clone(value)
    return clone if unsafe(segs)

    remove_in(clone, segs, 0)
    clone
  end

  def remove_in(cur, segs, i)
    s = segs[i]
    if i == segs.length - 1
      if cur.is_a?(Array) && s[0].nil? && s[1] < cur.length then cur.delete_at(s[1])
      elsif cur.is_a?(Hash) then cur.delete(seg_key(s))
      end
      return
    end
    nxt = if cur.is_a?(Hash) then cur[seg_key(s)]
          elsif cur.is_a?(Array) && s[0].nil? && s[1] < cur.length then cur[s[1]]
          end
    remove_in(nxt, segs, i + 1) if container(nxt)
  end

  def spread(v)
    case v
    when Hash then v
    when Array then v.each_with_index.to_h { |x, i| [i.to_s, x] }
    when String then units(v).each_with_index.to_h { |c, i| [i.to_s, from_units([c])] }
    else {}
    end
  end

  # Shallow merge, B over A.
  def merge(a, b)
    spread(a).merge(spread(b))
  end

  # A new object: target path from source path.
  def transform(source, mapping)
    out = {}
    as_array(mapping).each do |pair|
      p = as_array(pair)
      out = set_path(out, p[0], lookup(source, str(p[1])))
    end
    out
  end

  PLACEHOLDER = /\{\{\s*([^}]+?)\s*\}\}/
  WHOLE_PLACEHOLDER = /\A\{\{\s*([^}]+?)\s*\}\}\z/

  # Fills {{path}} placeholders from data.
  def template(value, data)
    r = fill(value, data)
    r.equal?(MISSING) ? nil : r
  end

  def fill(value, data)
    case value
    when String
      m = WHOLE_PLACEHOLDER.match(value)
      return lookup(data, m[1]) if m

      value.gsub(PLACEHOLDER) do
        r = get_path(data, Regexp.last_match(1))
        r.nil? ? '' : (container(r) ? json(r) : js_string(r))
      end
    when Array
      value.map do |x|
        z = fill(x, data)
        z.equal?(MISSING) ? nil : z
      end
    when Hash
      value.each_with_object({}) do |(k, x), o|
        z = fill(x, data)
        o[k] = z unless z.equal?(MISSING)
      end
    else value
    end
  end

  # JSON.parse that fails with INVALID_JSON.
  def parse_json(text)
    FddJson.parse(js_string(text))
  end

  # The { code, message } a Catch or Failed pin receives; an FddStop is raised again.
  def to_error(e)
    raise e if e.is_a?(FddStop)
    return obj('code', e.code, 'message', e.message) if e.is_a?(FddError)

    obj('code', 'RUNTIME_ERROR', 'message', e.message)
  end

  # ---------- strings ----------

  # A string operand: nil is "".
  def str(v)
    v.nil? ? '' : js_string(v)
  end

  # String(v), like a Switch compares.
  def as_string(v)
    js_string(v)
  end

  def contains(text, search)
    str(text).b.include?(str(search).b)
  end

  def starts_with(text, prefix)
    str(text).b.start_with?(str(prefix).b)
  end

  def ends_with(text, suffix)
    str(text).b.end_with?(str(suffix).b)
  end

  def trim(text)
    js_trim(str(text))
  end

  def lower(text)
    str(text).downcase
  end

  def upper(text)
    str(text).upcase
  end

  def str_length(text)
    units(str(text)).length.to_f
  end

  def concat(a, b)
    str(a) + str(b)
  end

  # text split on a separator (an empty one splits every UTF-16 unit, like JavaScript)
  def split_units(t, s)
    return units(t).map { |c| from_units([c]) } if s.empty?

    return [''] if t.empty?

    # a Regexp: split(" ") would split on runs of white space
    t.b.split(Regexp.new(Regexp.escape(s.b)), -1).map { |x| x.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8) }
  end

  def replace_all(text, search, replacement)
    split_units(str(text), str(search)).join(str(replacement))
  end

  # An empty separator splits on ",".
  def split(text, separator)
    s = str(separator)
    split_units(str(text), s.empty? ? ',' : s)
  end

  def join(items, separator)
    as_array(items).map { |x| str(x) }.join(str(separator))
  end

  # a JavaScript pattern as a Ruby one: without m, ^ and $ are the ends of the text (Ruby's are always line ends);
  # s lets . match a line end (Ruby's m)
  def js_regexp(pattern, flags)
    out = String.new
    in_class = false
    i = 0
    while i < pattern.length
      c = pattern[i]
      if c == '\\'
        out << c << (pattern[i + 1] || '')
        i += 2
        next
      end
      in_class = true if c == '[' && !in_class
      in_class = false if c == ']' && in_class
      out << (!in_class && !flags.include?('m') && c == '^' ? '\\A' : !in_class && !flags.include?('m') && c == '$' ? '\\z' : c)
      i += 1
    end
    opts = (flags.include?('i') ? Regexp::IGNORECASE : 0) | (flags.include?('s') ? Regexp::MULTILINE : 0)
    Regexp.new(out, opts)
  end

  def regex_match(text, pattern, flags)
    f = str(flags)
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_REGEX', "Invalid pattern #{str(pattern)}") if f.match?(/[^gimsuyd]/)

    begin
      re = js_regexp(str(pattern), f)
    rescue RegexpError
      raise FddError.new('INVALID_REGEX', "Invalid pattern #{str(pattern)}")
    end
    m = re.match(str(text))
    obj('matches', !m.nil?, 'groups', m ? m.captures : [])
  end

  # Fills {name} placeholders.
  def format(template, values)
    str(template).gsub(/\{(\w+)\}/) { str(get(values, Regexp.last_match(1))) }
  end

  # ---------- collections ----------

  def len(a)
    a.is_a?(Array) ? a.length.to_f : 0.0
  end

  def at(a, i)
    key_of(as_array(a), to_num(i))
  end

  # A copy with the item appended.
  def append(a, x)
    as_array(a) + [x]
  end

  # Deep-equal membership.
  def includes(a, x)
    as_array(a).any? { |y| deep_equal(y, x) }
  end

  def sum(a, path)
    p = str(path)
    as_array(a).sum(0.0) { |x| to_num(p.empty? ? x : get_path(x, p)) }
  end

  def sort_by(a, path, desc)
    dir = truthy(desc) ? -1 : 1
    p = str(path)
    # a stable merge sort, like Array.prototype.sort
    merge_sort(as_array(a)) do |x, y|
      u = p.empty? ? x : get_path(x, p)
      w = p.empty? ? y : get_path(y, p)
      lt(u, w) ? -dir : (lt(w, u) ? dir : 0)
    end
  end

  def merge_sort(l, &c)
    return l.dup if l.length < 2

    a = merge_sort(l[0, l.length / 2], &c)
    b = merge_sort(l[(l.length / 2)..], &c)
    out = []
    i = j = 0
    while i < a.length && j < b.length
      if c.call(b[j], a[i]).negative?
        out << b[j]
        j += 1
      else
        out << a[i]
        i += 1
      end
    end
    out + a[i..] + b[j..]
  end

  # The first item, or nil.
  def first(a)
    as_array(a).first
  end

  # The last item, or nil.
  def last(a)
    as_array(a).last
  end

  # Groups items by the text of a path: { value: [items] }.
  def group_by(a, path)
    p = str(path)
    groups = {}
    as_array(a).each { |x| (groups[to_string_value(p.empty? ? x : get_path(x, p))] ||= []) << x }
    key_list(groups).to_h { |k| [k, groups[k]] }
  end

  # The mean of numbers or of a path; 0 for an empty list.
  def average(a, path)
    n = as_array(a).length
    n.zero? ? 0.0 : sum(a, path) / n
  end

  # ---------- validation: every check returns { valid, message } ----------

  def valid
    obj('valid', true, 'message', '')
  end

  def invalid(message)
    obj('valid', false, 'message', message)
  end

  def check_required(v, field)
    is_empty(v) ? invalid("#{str(field)} is required") : valid
  end

  def check_email(v, field)
    v.is_a?(String) && v.match?(/\A[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+\z/) ? valid : invalid("#{str(field)} must be a valid email")
  end

  def value_type(v)
    case v
    when nil then 'null'
    when Array then 'array'
    when Integer then 'integer'
    when Float then v.finite? && v.floor == v ? 'integer' : 'number'
    when String then 'string'
    when true, false then 'boolean'
    else 'object'
    end
  end

  def check_type(v, type, field)
    vt = value_type(v)
    t = str(type)
    vt == t || (t == 'number' && vt == 'integer') ? valid : invalid("#{str(field)} must be #{t}")
  end

  # The first problem of a value against a shape, or nil.
  def check_value(v, s, path)
    return nil if !s.is_a?(Hash) || eq(get(s, 'type'), 'any')

    type = get(s, 'type')
    return truthy(get(s, 'nullable')) || eq(type, 'null') ? nil : "#{path} is null" if v.nil?

    t = value_type(v)
    return nil if eq(type, 'number') && %w[integer number].include?(t)
    return "#{path}: expected #{str(type)}, got #{t}" unless eq(type, t)

    en = get(s, 'enum')
    return "#{path}: #{json(v)} is not one of #{en.map { |x| js_string(x) }.join(', ')}" if en.is_a?(Array) && !en.empty? && !includes(en, v)

    props = get(s, 'properties')
    if props.is_a?(Hash) && v.is_a?(Hash)
      key_list(props).each do |k|
        unless v.key?(k)
          return "#{path}.#{k} is missing" if truthy(get(props[k], 'required'))

          next
        end
        p = check_value(v[k], props[k], "#{path}.#{k}")
        return p unless p.nil?
      end
    end
    if v.is_a?(Array)
      v.each_with_index do |x, i|
        p = check_value(x, get(s, 'items'), "#{path}[#{i}]")
        return p unless p.nil?
      end
    end
    nil
  end

  def check_shape(v, shape, field)
    p = check_value(v, shape, str(field))
    p.nil? ? valid : invalid(p)
  end

  def check_range(v, lo, hi, field)
    return invalid("#{str(field)} must be a number") unless v.is_a?(Numeric)
    return invalid("#{str(field)} must be ≥ #{js_string(lo)}") if !lo.nil? && !eq(lo, '') && v < to_num(lo)
    return invalid("#{str(field)} must be ≤ #{js_string(hi)}") if !hi.nil? && !eq(hi, '') && v > to_num(hi)

    valid
  end

  def check_regex(v, pattern, field)
    re = begin
      js_regexp(str(pattern), '')
    rescue RegexpError
      return invalid('invalid pattern')
    end
    re.match?(str(v)) ? valid : invalid("#{str(field)} has an invalid format")
  end

  def check_password(v, policy, field)
    p = str(v)
    min = to_num(get(policy, 'minLength'))
    return invalid("#{str(field)} must be at least #{num_text(min)} characters") if units(p).length < min
    return invalid("#{str(field)} must contain a digit") if truthy(get(policy, 'requireDigit')) && !p.match?(/[0-9]/)
    return invalid("#{str(field)} must contain an uppercase letter") if truthy(get(policy, 'requireUpper')) && !p.match?(/[A-Z]/)

    valid
  end

  # ---------- conversion ----------

  # Objects become JSON.
  def to_string_value(v)
    return json(v) if container(v)

    v.nil? ? '' : js_string(v)
  end

  # Not a number is 0.
  def to_number(v)
    n = js_number(v)
    n.nan? ? 0.0 : n
  end

  def is_numeric(v)
    !js_number(v).nan?
  end

  def to_boolean(v)
    truthy(v)
  end

  # string, integer, number, boolean, object, array or null.
  def type_of(v)
    value_type(v)
  end

  # ---------- math ----------

  # Math.min and Math.max: NaN wins, -0 is below 0.
  def js_min(a, b)
    return Float::NAN if a.nan? || b.nan?
    return (1.0 / a).negative? ? a : b if a == b

    a < b ? a : b
  end

  def js_max(a, b)
    return Float::NAN if a.nan? || b.nan?
    return (1.0 / a).negative? ? b : a if a == b

    a > b ? a : b
  end

  # 0-15 decimals, halves up.
  def round(v, decimals)
    x = to_num(v)
    d = trunc(to_num(decimals))
    f = 10.0**(d.finite? ? d.clamp(0, 15).to_i : 0)
    y = (x * f) + 0.5
    y.finite? ? y.floor.to_f / f : x
  end

  def floor(v)
    x = to_num(v)
    x.finite? ? x.floor.to_f : x
  end

  def ceil(v)
    x = to_num(v)
    x.finite? ? x.ceil.to_f : x
  end

  def abs(v)
    to_num(v).abs
  end

  def min(a, b)
    js_min(to_num(a), to_num(b))
  end

  def max(a, b)
    js_max(to_num(a), to_num(b))
  end

  # Keeps the value between lo and hi.
  def clamp(v, lo, hi)
    js_min(js_max(to_num(v), to_num(lo)), to_num(hi))
  end

  # JavaScript's ** (1 ** Infinity is NaN).
  def power(a, b)
    x = to_num(a)
    y = to_num(b)
    return Float::NAN if y.nan? || (x.abs == 1 && y.infinite?)

    r = x**y
    r.is_a?(Complex) ? Float::NAN : r.to_f
  end

  def sqrt(v)
    x = to_num(v)
    x.negative? || x.nan? ? Float::NAN : Math.sqrt(x)
  end

  # ---------- text and encoding ----------

  # A slice position: negative counts from the end, clamped to 0..n.
  def rel_index(v, n)
    r = trunc(to_num(v))
    return 0 if r.nan?

    r.negative? ? [n + r, 0].max.to_i : [r, n].min.to_i
  end

  # Like String.prototype.slice; a nil end means the end of the text.
  def substring(text, start, finish)
    u = units(str(text))
    i = rel_index(start, u.length)
    j = finish.nil? ? u.length : rel_index(finish, u.length)
    j <= i ? '' : from_units(u[i...j])
  end

  def index_of(text, search)
    unit_index(units(str(text)), units(str(search))).to_f
  end

  def pad(text, length, fill, at_start)
    t = str(text)
    n = trunc(to_num(length))
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_LENGTH', 'Length must be at most 100000') if n > 100_000

    f = units(fill.nil? ? ' ' : str(fill))
    tu = units(t)
    return t if n.nan? || n <= tu.length || f.empty?

    need = n.to_i - tu.length
    p = from_units((f * ((need / f.length) + 1))[0, need])
    at_start ? p + t : t + p
  end

  def pad_start(text, length, fill)
    pad(text, length, fill, true)
  end

  def pad_end(text, length, fill)
    pad(text, length, fill, false)
  end

  # UTF-8 text as Base64.
  def base64_encode(text)
    [str(text)].pack('m0')
  end

  # Base64 as UTF-8 text; fails with INVALID_BASE64.
  def base64_decode(text)
    t = str(text).gsub(/[\t\n\f\r ]+/, '')
    t = t.sub(/={1,2}\z/, '') if (t.length % 4).zero?
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_BASE64', 'Not valid Base64') if t.length % 4 == 1 || !t.match?(%r{\A[A-Za-z0-9+/]*\z})

    # invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD, like TextDecoder
    (t + ('=' * ((4 - (t.length % 4)) % 4))).unpack1('m').force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub("�")
  end

  # Fixed decimals (halves up) and a thousands separator; fails with INVALID_NUMBER.
  def format_number(value, decimals, thousands, point)
    d0 = trunc(to_num(decimals))
    d = d0.finite? ? d0.clamp(0, 15).to_i : 0
    r = round(value, d.to_f)
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_NUMBER', 'Not a number that can be formatted') if !r.finite? || r.abs >= 1e21

    whole, frac = Kernel.format("%.#{d}f", r.abs).split('.')
    frac ||= ''
    sign = r.negative? && (whole + frac).match?(/[1-9]/) ? '-' : ''
    sign + whole.reverse.scan(/\d{1,3}/).join(str(thousands).reverse).reverse + (frac.empty? ? '' : str(point) + frac)
  end

  # sha256, sha1 or md5 ("SHA-256" too); fails with INVALID_ALGORITHM.
  def digest_algorithm(a)
    k = js_trim(str(a)).downcase.delete('-')
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_ALGORITHM', "Unknown hash algorithm \"#{str(a)}\" (use sha256, sha1 or md5)") unless %w[sha256 sha1 md5].include?(k)

    { 'sha256' => Digest::SHA256, 'sha1' => Digest::SHA1, 'md5' => Digest::MD5 }[k]
  end

  # hex or base64; fails with INVALID_ENCODING.
  def encode_digest(raw, encoding)
    case js_trim(str(encoding)).downcase
    when 'hex' then raw.unpack1('H*')
    when 'base64' then [raw].pack('m0')
    else raise FddError.new('INVALID_ENCODING', "Unknown encoding \"#{str(encoding)}\" (use hex or base64)")
    end
  end

  # SHA-256, SHA-1 or MD5 of UTF-8 text, as hex or Base64.
  def hash_text(text, algorithm, encoding)
    encode_digest(digest_algorithm(algorithm).digest(str(text)), encoding)
  end

  # The HMAC of UTF-8 text with a UTF-8 key, as hex or Base64.
  def hmac(text, key, algorithm, encoding)
    d = digest_algorithm(algorithm)
    k = str(key).b
    k = d.digest(k) if k.bytesize > 64
    k = k.ljust(64, "\0")
    inner = d.digest(k.bytes.map { |x| x ^ 0x36 }.pack('C*') + str(text).b)
    encode_digest(d.digest(k.bytes.map { |x| x ^ 0x5c }.pack('C*') + inner), encoding)
  end

  # encodeURIComponent.
  def url_encode(text)
    str(text).b.gsub(/[^A-Za-z0-9\-_.!~*'()]/n) { |c| "%#{c.unpack1('H2').upcase}" }.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
  end

  # decodeURIComponent; fails with INVALID_URL_ENCODING.
  def url_decode(text)
    s = str(text)
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_URL_ENCODING', 'Not valid URL encoding') if s.match?(/%(?![0-9a-fA-F]{2})/)

    out = s.b.gsub(/%([0-9a-fA-F]{2})/n) { Regexp.last_match(1).hex.chr }.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_URL_ENCODING', 'Not valid URL encoding') if !out.valid_encoding? && s.valid_encoding?

    out
  end

  # ---------- records and lists ----------

  def index_key(k)
    k.match?(/\A(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\z/) && k.to_f < 4_294_967_295
  end

  # Field names in JavaScript's order: integer-like keys ascending, then the rest as inserted.
  def key_list(o)
    return [] unless o.is_a?(Hash)

    ks = o.keys.map(&:to_s)
    ks.select { |k| index_key(k) }.sort_by(&:to_f) + ks.reject { |k| index_key(k) }
  end

  def keys(o)
    key_list(o)
  end

  def values(o)
    key_list(o).map { |k| o[k] }
  end

  def entries(o)
    key_list(o).map { |k| obj('key', k, 'value', o[k]) }
  end

  # Like Array.prototype.slice; a nil end means the end of the list.
  def slice(a, start, finish)
    l = as_array(a)
    i = rel_index(start, l.length)
    j = finish.nil? ? l.length : rel_index(finish, l.length)
    j <= i ? [] : l[i...j]
  end

  def reverse(a)
    as_array(a).reverse
  end

  # Removes deep-equal duplicates, the first kept.
  def unique(a)
    as_array(a).each_with_object([]) { |x, out| out << x unless includes(out, x) }
  end

  # The deep-equal position, or -1.
  def item_index(a, x)
    (as_array(a).index { |y| deep_equal(y, x) } || -1).to_f
  end

  # Flattens one level.
  def flatten(a)
    as_array(a).flat_map { |x| x.is_a?(Array) ? x : [x] }
  end

  # ---------- dates: ISO 8601 text in UTC; numbers are epoch milliseconds ----------

  MIN_MS = -62_167_219_200_000
  MAX_MS = 253_402_300_799_999
  DAY_MS = 86_400_000
  TIME_UNITS = { 'millisecond' => 1, 'milliseconds' => 1, 'ms' => 1, 'second' => 1000, 'seconds' => 1000, 'minute' => 60_000, 'minutes' => 60_000,
                 'hour' => 3_600_000, 'hours' => 3_600_000, 'day' => DAY_MS, 'days' => DAY_MS, 'week' => 7 * DAY_MS, 'weeks' => 7 * DAY_MS,
                 'month' => -1, 'months' => -1, 'year' => -12, 'years' => -12 }.freeze
  MONTHS = %w[January February March April May June July August September October November December].freeze
  DAYS = %w[Sunday Monday Tuesday Wednesday Thursday Friday Saturday].freeze
  DATE_TOKENS = %w[yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h mm m ss s SSS a].freeze
  DATE_TEXT = /\A([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})(?:[Tt ]([0-9]{2}):([0-9]{2})(?::([0-9]{2})(?:\.([0-9]+))?)?)?(?:([Zz])|([+-])([0-9]{2}):?([0-9]{2}))?\z/

  # Days since 1970-01-01 (proleptic Gregorian).
  def days_from_civil(y, m, d)
    y -= 1 if m <= 2
    era = y.div(400)
    yoe = y - (era * 400)
    doy = (((153 * (m > 2 ? m - 3 : m + 9)) + 2) / 5) + d - 1
    (era * 146_097) + (yoe * 365) + (yoe / 4) - (yoe / 100) + doy - 719_468
  end

  def civil_from_days(z)
    z += 719_468
    era = z.div(146_097)
    doe = z - (era * 146_097)
    yoe = (doe - (doe / 1460) + (doe / 36_524) - (doe / 146_096)) / 365
    doy = doe - ((365 * yoe) + (yoe / 4) - (yoe / 100))
    mp = ((5 * doy) + 2) / 153
    m = mp < 10 ? mp + 3 : mp - 9
    [yoe + (era * 400) + (m <= 2 ? 1 : 0), m, doy - (((153 * mp) + 2) / 5) + 1]
  end

  def days_in(y, m)
    return y % 4 == 0 && (y % 100 != 0 || y % 400 == 0) ? 29 : 28 if m == 2

    [4, 6, 9, 11].include?(m) ? 30 : 31
  end

  # The epoch milliseconds of a date (years 0-9999), or nil.
  def date_ms(v)
    if v.is_a?(Numeric)
      x = v.to_f
      return nil if !x.finite? || trunc(x) < MIN_MS || trunc(x) > MAX_MS

      return trunc(x).to_i
    end
    return nil unless v.is_a?(String)

    m = DATE_TEXT.match(js_trim(v))
    return nil unless m

    g = ->(k) { m[k].to_i }
    y, mo, d, h, mi, sec = (1..6).map { |k| g.(k) }
    return nil if mo < 1 || mo > 12 || d < 1 || d > days_in(y, mo) || h > 23 || mi > 59 || sec > 59

    tz = !m[9].nil?
    return nil if tz && (g.(10) > 23 || g.(11) > 59)

    off = tz ? (g.(10) * 60) + g.(11) : 0
    off = -off if m[9] == '-'
    frac = "#{m[7]}000"[0, 3].to_i
    ms = ((((days_from_civil(y, mo, d) * 86_400) + (h * 3600) + (mi * 60) + sec) * 1000) + frac) - (off * 60_000)
    ms.between?(MIN_MS, MAX_MS) ? ms : nil
  end

  def need_date(v)
    date_ms(v) || raise(FddError.new('INVALID_DATE', 'Not a valid date'))
  end

  # [year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond, weekday (0 = Sunday), time of day]
  def date_fields(ms)
    days = ms.div(DAY_MS)
    t = ms - (days * DAY_MS)
    y, m, d = civil_from_days(days)
    [y, m, d, t / 3_600_000, (t / 60_000) % 60, (t / 1000) % 60, t % 1000, (days + 4) % 7, t]
  end

  def iso_date(ms)
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_DATE', 'The date is out of range') unless ms >= MIN_MS && ms <= MAX_MS

    p = date_fields(ms.to_i)
    Kernel.format('%04d-%02d-%02dT%02d:%02d:%02d.%03dZ', *p[0, 7])
  end

  # The milliseconds of a unit; months are -1 and years -12.
  def time_unit(u)
    TIME_UNITS[js_trim(str(u)).downcase] || raise(FddError.new('INVALID_UNIT', "Unknown time unit \"#{str(u)}\""))
  end

  # A date as UTC date-time text and epoch milliseconds.
  def parse_date(v)
    ms = date_ms(v)
    return obj('date', nil, 'timestamp', nil, 'valid', false) if ms.nil?

    obj('date', iso_date(ms.to_f), 'timestamp', ms.to_f, 'valid', true)
  end

  def z(n, w)
    n.to_s.rjust(w, '0')
  end

  # yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h mm m ss s SSS a; text in single quotes is kept as is, and two single quotes are one.
  def format_date(date, pattern)
    p = date_fields(need_date(date))
    f = str(pattern)
    h12 = (p[3] % 12).zero? ? 12 : p[3] % 12
    month = MONTHS[p[1] - 1]
    day = DAYS[p[7]]
    vals = [z(p[0], 4), z(p[0] % 100, 2), month, month[0, 3], z(p[1], 2), p[1].to_s, z(p[2], 2), p[2].to_s, day, day[0, 3],
            z(p[3], 2), p[3].to_s, z(h12, 2), h12.to_s, z(p[4], 2), p[4].to_s, z(p[5], 2), p[5].to_s, z(p[6], 3), p[3] < 12 ? 'AM' : 'PM']
    out = String.new
    i = 0
    while i < f.length
      if f[i] == "'"
        if f[i + 1] == "'"
          out << "'"
          i += 2
          next
        end
        i += 1
        while i < f.length
          if f[i] != "'" then out << f[i]
          elsif f[i + 1] == "'"
            out << "'"
            i += 1
          else break
          end
          i += 1
        end
        i += 1
        next
      end
      k = DATE_TOKENS.index { |t| f[i, t.length] == t }
      if k
        out << vals[k]
        i += DATE_TOKENS[k].length
      else
        out << f[i]
        i += 1
      end
    end
    out
  end

  # Months and years keep the day, clamped to the end of the month.
  def add_time(date, amount, unit)
    ms = need_date(date)
    u = time_unit(unit)
    n = to_num(amount)
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_DATE', 'The date is out of range') unless n.finite?
    return iso_date(ms + ((n * u) + 0.5).floor) if u.positive?
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_DATE', 'The date is out of range') if trunc(n).abs > 1e6

    p = date_fields(ms)
    total = (p[0] * 12) + p[1] - 1 + (trunc(n).to_i * -u)
    y = total.div(12)
    m = total - (y * 12) + 1
    iso_date(((days_from_civil(y, m, [p[2], days_in(y, m)].min) * DAY_MS) + p[8]).to_f)
  end

  # Whole units from From to To, toward zero.
  def time_between(from, to, unit)
    a = need_date(from)
    b = need_date(to)
    u = time_unit(unit)
    return trunc((b - a).to_f / u) + 0.0 if u.positive?

    p = date_fields(a)
    q = date_fields(b)
    months = ((q[0] - p[0]) * 12) + q[1] - p[1]
    if months.positive? && (q[2] < p[2] || (q[2] == p[2] && q[8] < p[8])) then months -= 1
    elsif months.negative? && (q[2] > p[2] || (q[2] == p[2] && q[8] > p[8])) then months += 1
    end
    trunc(months.to_f / -u) + 0.0
  end

  # year ... millisecond in UTC, weekday 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.
  def date_parts(date)
    p = date_fields(need_date(date))
    obj('year', p[0].to_f, 'month', p[1].to_f, 'day', p[2].to_f, 'hour', p[3].to_f, 'minute', p[4].to_f, 'second', p[5].to_f,
        'millisecond', p[6].to_f, 'weekday', (p[7].zero? ? 7 : p[7]).to_f)
  end

  # A UTC date-time from its parts; fails with INVALID_DATE.
  def make_date(year, month, day, hour, minute, second)
    v = [year, month, day, hour, minute, second].map { |x| to_num(x) }
    raise FddError.new('INVALID_DATE', 'Not a valid date') if v.any? { |x| !x.finite? || x.floor != x || x.abs > 1e15 }

    y, m, d, h, mi, s = v.map(&:to_i)
    if y.negative? || y > 9999 || m < 1 || m > 12 || d < 1 || d > days_in(y, m) || h.negative? || h > 23 || mi.negative? || mi > 59 || s.negative? || s > 59
      raise FddError.new('INVALID_DATE', 'Not a valid date')
    end

    iso_date((((days_from_civil(y, m, d) * 86_400) + (h * 3600) + (mi * 60) + s) * 1000).to_f)
  end

  # The first (or last) millisecond of the hour, day, week from Monday, month or year.
  def period_edge(date, unit, finish)
    ms = need_date(date)
    p = date_fields(ms)
    day = ms - p[8]
    from, length = case js_trim(str(unit)).downcase
                   when 'hour', 'hours' then [ms - (p[8] % 3_600_000), 3_600_000]
                   when 'day', 'days' then [day, DAY_MS]
                   when 'week', 'weeks' then [day - (((p[7] + 6) % 7) * DAY_MS), 7 * DAY_MS]
                   when 'month', 'months' then [days_from_civil(p[0], p[1], 1) * DAY_MS, days_in(p[0], p[1]) * DAY_MS]
                   when 'year', 'years'
                     [days_from_civil(p[0], 1, 1) * DAY_MS, (days_from_civil(p[0] + 1, 1, 1) - days_from_civil(p[0], 1, 1)) * DAY_MS]
                   else raise FddError.new('INVALID_UNIT', "Unknown period \"#{str(unit)}\" (use hour, day, week, month or year)")
                   end
    iso_date((finish ? from + length - 1 : from).to_f)
  end

  # The first moment of the period the date is in (UTC).
  def start_of(date, unit)
    period_edge(date, unit, false)
  end

  # The last moment (...:59.999) of the period the date is in (UTC).
  def end_of(date, unit)
    period_edge(date, unit, true)
  end

  # ---------- runtime ----------

  # The current date-time (ISO, like JavaScript's toISOString).
  def now
    iso_date((Time.now.to_r * 1000).floor.to_f)
  end

  def uuid
    b = Random.urandom(16).bytes
    b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0f) | 0x40
    b[8] = (b[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80
    h = b.pack('C*').unpack1('H*')
    "#{h[0, 8]}-#{h[8, 4]}-#{h[12, 4]}-#{h[16, 4]}-#{h[20, 12]}"
  end

  # An integer between min and max.
  def random(min, max)
    a = to_num(min)
    b = to_num(max)
    (a + (Kernel.rand * (b - a + 1))).floor.to_f
  end

  def log(message)
    warn(message.is_a?(String) ? message : json(message))
    nil
  end

  def sleep(ms)
    Kernel.sleep([0, to_num(ms)].max / 1000.0)
    nil
  end

  # A Parallel step: each branch (a lambda) on a thread of its own; when all are done, the first failing branch's error
  # (in branch order) if one failed. Waits on boundaries (network, files) overlap; Ruby code itself runs one at a time.
  def parallel(*branches)
    threads = branches.map do |b|
      Thread.new do
        Thread.current.report_on_exception = false
        b.call
        nil
      end
    end
    failures = threads.map do |t|
      t.join
      nil
    rescue Exception => e # rubocop:disable Lint/RescueException -- every failure is passed on, a stop too
      e
    end
    first = failures.compact.first
    raise first if first

    nil
  end
end

module FddJob0
  extend ::FddRuntime

  def self.sign_in(request, deps)
    __f = ::FddVerify.frame("bp-auth-login")
    __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-001")
    email = get(get(request, "body"), "email")
    email_check = check_email(email, "email")
    password = get(get(request, "body"), "password")
    __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-006")
    if !(bool(get(email_check, "valid")) && !is_empty(password))
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-009")
      return obj(
        "status", 401.0,
        "body", obj(
          "error", bool(get(email_check, "valid")) ? get(check_required(password, "password"), "message") : get(email_check, "message")
        )
      )
    end
    __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-010")
    look_up_user = ::FddVerify.dep("userService", "getUsersByEmail", "NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-010", [obj("query", omit_nulls(obj("email", email)))])
    status1 = get(look_up_user, "status")
    if eq(status1, 200.0)
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-014")
      if !eq(get(get(look_up_user, "body"), "passwordHash"), format("hash:{password}", obj("password", password)))
        __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-021")
        return obj("status", 401.0, "body", obj("error", "Invalid credentials"))
      end
      id = get(get(look_up_user, "body"), "id")
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-018")
      ::FddVerify.dep("eventBus", "publishUserLoggedIn", "NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-018", [obj("userId", id)])
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-019")
      return obj(
        "status", 200.0,
        "body", obj(
          "accessToken", format("TEST-TOKEN-{id}", obj("id", id)),
          "refreshToken", "REFRESH-TOKEN",
          "expiresIn", 3600.0,
          "tokenType", "Bearer"
        )
      )
    elsif eq(status1, 404.0)
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-022")
      return obj("status", 401.0, "body", obj("error", "Invalid credentials"))
    else
      __f.enter("NODE-AUTH-LOGIN-023")
      raise FddError.new("UPSTREAM_ERROR", "User Service failed")
    end
  end
